answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may place jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. The wharf may host a public registry of deposits, while a mirror service checks that one operator is not quietly reusing credentials across accounts; a zephyr of fresh aliases gains no extra influence without fresh capital. Sybils remain possible, but multiplying them ties up funds and multiplies the amount at risk.
